subcategory_description: How much of your savings is protected if a bank fails, and government-backed savings schemes.
subject_intro: How much of your savings the Financial Services Compensation Scheme protects if your bank, building society or credit union fails, including temporary high balances.
subject_meta_description: The FSCS protects savings up to £120,000 if a UK bank, building society or credit union fails, and temporary high balances up to £1.4 million.
label: Deposit protection limit
context: The FSCS compensates eligible savers up to this if a UK bank, building society or credit union fails on or after 1 December 2025.

label: Temporary high balance limit
context: Higher protection for a short-term large balance, such as money from a house sale. No limit applies to payments for personal injury or incapacity.

subject_intro: A government-backed savings account for certain people receiving Universal Credit, which pays a 50% bonus on what you save over 4 years.
subject_meta_title: Help to Save: £50 a Month, Up to £1,200 Bonus
subject_meta_description: Help to Save for Universal Credit claimants: save up to £50 a month and get a 50% government bonus, worth up to £1,200 over 4 years.
label: Most you can pay in each month
context: You can save between £1 and this each calendar month, and you don't have to pay in every month.

label: Bonus rate
context: Bonuses are paid after 2 and 4 years, based on the highest balance you've saved. They're tax-free and paid into your bank account.

label: Most you can pay in over 4 years
context: The total if you pay in the full monthly amount for the whole 4 years.

label: Most you can earn in bonuses
context: You keep any bonus you've earned even if you withdraw money, but withdrawals make it harder to earn the full amount.

label: How long the account lasts
context: The account closes 4 years after you open it, and you can't open another one.

subject_intro: The current interest rates on NS&I's savings accounts and British Savings Bonds. NS&I is backed by HM Treasury, so your savings are protected in full.
subject_meta_title: NS&I Interest Rates: Direct Saver, Income Bonds and Savings Bonds
subject_meta_description: Current NS&I rates for Direct Saver, Income Bonds, Direct ISA, Junior ISA and the 1, 2, 3 and 5-year British Savings Bonds.
label: Direct Saver
context: Variable rate before tax, with interest added once a year. You can open it with £1 or more.

label: Income Bonds (AER)
context: Variable. Interest is paid monthly at 3.69% gross. You can open it with £500 or more.

label: Direct ISA
context: Variable tax-free rate. You can open it with £1 or more.

label: Junior ISA
context: Variable tax-free rate for a child's savings. You can open it with £1 or more.

label: British Savings Bond, 1-year fixed
context: Guaranteed Growth Bonds Issue 93, AER. The rate is fixed for the term and the interest is taxable. You can open it with £500 or more.

label: British Savings Bond, 2-year fixed
context: Guaranteed Growth Bonds Issue 81, AER. The rate is fixed for the term and the interest is taxable. You can open it with £500 or more.

label: British Savings Bond, 3-year fixed
context: Guaranteed Growth Bonds Issue 83, AER. The rate is fixed for the term and the interest is taxable. You can open it with £500 or more.

label: British Savings Bond, 5-year fixed
context: Guaranteed Growth Bonds Issue 75, AER. The rate is fixed for the term and the interest is taxable. You can open it with £500 or more.

label: Green Savings Bonds, 3-year fixed
context: Issue 9. The rate is fixed for 3 years and the interest is taxable. You can open it with £100 or more.
Premium Bonds pay prizes rather than interest. This is the average rate across all prizes, and prizes are tax-free.
NS&I's Junior ISA rate, as one example of what a cash Junior ISA pays.

label: Cash ISA limit for under-65s from 6 April 2027
context: Within the overall £20,000 ISA allowance. People aged 65 and over can still put up to £20,000 a year into cash ISAs.

label: Basic rate on savings income from April 2027
context: Interest above your tax-free allowances will be taxed at this rate from 6 April 2027, up from 20%.

label: Higher rate on savings income from April 2027
context: Up from 40%. The Personal Savings Allowance and starting rate for savings stay the same.

label: Additional rate on savings income from April 2027
context: Up from 45%.
